Implementation complete and verified locally. Here's the summary.

## Result
- Goal/task: `G-…4459a890` / `T-20260805T034218808409Z-0f0d9640` — make a granted lock a precondition of dispatch
- Role: Implementer (TDD)
- Status: ready (implementation done + locally verified; the Shiki loop owns commit/push/PR/CCA/MergeGate)

## What changed
A task could be dispatched, implemented, and merged while its lock grant did not exist — the only signal appeared three steps downstream as an unexplained Guardian demand at closeout. Now a granted lock is enforced at dispatch.

- **`scripts/shiki_tasks.py`**
  - `evaluate_lock_grant` rewritten as a **pure, side-effect-free** predicate `(granted, reason)`: empty locks → vacuously granted; otherwise the record must exist, be readable (via `load_lock_record`, so malformed → refuse, not crash), be `state:active`, and cover every declared lock. Refusals name the task, the missing/stale locks, and any conflicting owner.
  - The amendment auto-refresh was **relocated** out of the predicate into a new `_refresh_amendment_grant` helper called only by `cmd_dispatch_check` (layered over the pure predicate; still emits the exact `grant/contract divergence` reason existing tests grep).
  - `cmd_task_status` refuses moving a task **into `ready`** when ungranted (same reason); other transitions untouched.
  - `cmd_lock_acquire` conflict path documented — returns non-zero, writes no record; that absence is the legible ungranted state the preconditions read.
- **`scripts/shiki_runtime.py`**: `dispatch_runner_task` refuses an ungranted task right after the status check (before any runner starts); `dispatchable_task_ids` excludes ungranted tasks; `cmd_runner_execute` only advertises `ready` when the grant holds — all via the shared predicate, none acquiring as a side effect.
- **Tests**: new `tests/test_dispatch_lock_precondition.py` (13 tests covering every acceptance check, incl. the 2026-08-04 conflicted-acquire→dispatch sequence and the "no side effect" invariant); updated `tests/test_lock_lifecycle.py` so its `cmd_dispatch_check` driver agrees with the pure predicate and keeps the amendment auto-refresh covered where it now lives.

## Checklist status
- Skill Gate: `tdd` (red → green), `code-review` (self-reviewed diff)
- TDD: new tests written failing first, then implemented to green
- CCA/MergeGate: not run locally (owned by the loop/GitHub)

## Evidence (local, diagnostic)
- Full Python suite: **982 tests, OK**
- New + lifecycle lock tests: **30 tests, OK**
- 5 required shell tests pass unchanged: `runner_claude`, `daemon_runner`, `loop_lock_guard`, `control_plane` (incl. amendment auto-refresh + divergence assertions), `goal_loop`; plus `runner_codex`, `code_review_gate`, `run_orchestrator`, `module_boundaries`, `state_classes`, `loop_e2e`
- `validate_shiki`: passed; `py_compile`: clean
- Changes strictly within declared locks; `.shiki/tasks|locks/*0f0d9640.json` are the loop's own pre-existing records (untouched)

## Next action
- Loop delivers (commit/push/PR with MergeGate body), then CCA judgment + MergeGate. No approval records were authored (none were mine to author).

One design note worth flagging for review: this task made `evaluate_lock_grant` pure and moved the merged amendment auto-refresh feature into `cmd_dispatch_check` (rather than removing it) — that keeps `test_shiki_control_plane.sh`'s amendment/divergence assertions green while satisfying the new "never acquires a lock as a side effect" requirement.
